module.title: Days 1–10 | Competition Mastery Module
module.description: Production candidate: authored topic-driven National Science Championship curriculum.

lessons.title: Experimental design
lessons.objective: Build competition-ready understanding of experimental design and apply it accurately to unfamiliar questions.
lessons.core_teaching_content: Advanced science questions require integration of experiment design, physics, chemistry, biology and Earth or space systems. Identify the measurable variables, relevant principle and evidence before calculating or concluding. Distinguish a model from an observation and a correlation from causation. Cross-disciplinary questions are best solved by decomposing the scenario into smaller scientific claims and checking each one. In this lesson, focus specifically on experimental design. Identify the defining concepts, the distinctions that commonly cause mistakes, and the evidence or procedure needed to justify an answer. Practise moving from recognition to application: first identify what the question is testing, then select a method, perform the reasoning carefully, and verify the result against the wording and constraints. Keep an error log that records the misconception or decision error, not just the correct answer.
examples: A National Science Championship question on experimental design should be solved by identifying the key clue, applying the relevant principle, and checking the option against all stated conditions.
Create a new experimental design scenario with one tempting distractor. Explain why the correct response is supported and why the distractor fails.
lessons.practical_activity: Complete a focused National Science Championship activity on experimental design. Build a small table, diagram, worked example, speaking sample, writing sample or practice set as appropriate to the subject, then explain the reasoning behind the result.
lessons.guided_practice: Work through three scaffolded tasks on experimental design: model the first, prompt the second, and require independent justification on the third. Ask the learner to identify the exact clue, rule or evidence used before confirming the answer.
independent_practice: Solve three unfamiliar questions on experimental design without viewing the answer.
Create one new example and solve it using the lesson method.
Review one distractor or error and explain why it is wrong.
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: Complete an eight-item National Science Championship checkpoint focused on experimental design. Target at least six correct and justify every uncertain response.
lessons.student_task: Produce one finished National Science Championship task demonstrating experimental design and record the reasoning, evidence or performance criteria used.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Coach the learner toward evidence-based reasoning and precise terminology. Ask for the method before giving correction, and turn each error into a reusable rule or practice target. This lesson remains suitable for self-learning.
lessons.reflection_completion: Record one strength, one mistake pattern and one concrete action for improving experimental design in the next practice session.
lessons.daily_flow: Learn → Worked Example → Guided Practice → Independent Practice → Check → Reflect
